title: Memory Hierarchy and Caches
notes: Two files in one week: lecture slides on the hierarchy and a worked-problems sheet on average access time. The formula appears only in the problem sheet, so a summary that reads only the slides cannot state it. Traps: cache coherence and prefetching, which neither file mentions.

pages.text:
Week 9 — Memory Hierarchy (slides).

Faster memory is smaller and more expensive: registers, then cache, then main memory, then disk. The hierarchy works because of locality. Temporal locality: recently used data is likely to be used again. Spatial locality: data near recently used data is likely to be used soon.

A cache hit finds the data in the cache; a miss goes to the next level. The hit rate is the fraction of accesses that hit. A cache holds blocks (lines) rather than single bytes, which exploits spatial locality.

Problem sheet 9.

Average memory access time (AMAT) = hit time + miss rate * miss penalty.

Q1: hit time 1 ns, miss rate 5%, miss penalty 100 ns. AMAT = 1 + 0.05 * 100 = 6 ns.

Q2: halving the miss rate to 2.5% gives AMAT = 1 + 0.025 * 100 = 3.5 ns.
